### Fixed
- **The substrate release pins the platform Harness's image in atelet's image cache, and the Substrate line re-pins to `v0.0.27-gs.6`** (giantswarm/giantswarm#37764; giantswarm/giantswarm#37742 rows 34 and 35): atelet's image GC evicted every image older than two minutes on every pass while the cache volume sat above the 85 % watermark — the Harness image included — so the first turn after a few idle minutes paid a cold pull and unpack that did not fit the resume's restore budget and failed with `context canceled`. The line's sixth release (giantswarm/substrate#21, #23, #24) makes the pinned set configurable (`--image-cache-pinned-images`; chart `atelet.imageCache.{gcPeriod,highPercent,lowPercent,minAge,maxBytes,pinnedImages}`, unset by default) and raises the router's request-parking budget to 30 s. The meta chart derives `atelet.imageCache.pinnedImages` for the `substrate` release from `kagent.harness.image` (`agent-platform.componentDerivedValues`, next to the CNPG connection Secret): the platform Harness's digest joins whatever `substrate.atelet.imageCache.pinnedImages` lists — the installation's own pins first, once each — so atelet pulls it at every GC pass and never evicts it, and a Harness re-pin moves the pinned set with it; no second copy of the digest anywhere. The other `imageCache` knobs stay the chart's defaults (an installation or a lab tunes them in `substrate.atelet.imageCache`). `components.substrate`/`components.substrate-crds` move to `>=0.0.27-gs.6 <0.0.28-0` and `kagent.substrateWorkerPool.workerImage` to `…:0.0.27-gs.6`; `examples/customer-bom.yaml` and `tests/verify-components.py` move with the pin. `make verify-components` asserts the derived pin (the default render, a re-pinned Harness image, an installation's own list). An installation on the 4.x line rolls the atelet DaemonSet once (`--image-cache-pinned-images=<Harness digest>`) on its next reconcile; the lab proof — no `Image cache evicting image record` for the Harness image, the first turn after ten idle minutes completing — is the audit's next step. **No installation acts** — the release stays inert behind the fleet's `<4.0.0` bound.
